work.title: SELF-PACED ROUTE
work.subtitle: 自主学习路线
work.scope: Fictional adult learning exercises. Illustrations are not records of real participants or research evidence. No accredited qualification or actual learner outcomes are supplied.

pages.title: Choose a useful starting point.
pages.lead: This self-paced course helps an adult learner practise reading and summarising a short fictional passage. Start by identifying which part of that task feels least clear.
pages.body: You may want practice locating a main idea, distinguishing an example from a claim or writing a concise summary. This self-check is a personal choice, not a diagnostic assessment.
pages.subheading: Current comfort / difficult step / chosen focus
pages.detail: Working record: Select one focus and describe it in observable terms. Keep your first attempt and your revised version so the change remains visible.
pages.question: Select one focus and describe it in observable terms.

pages.title: Set a small learning goal.
pages.lead: A useful goal describes an action you can review in your own work. Avoid a broad promise such as become an excellent reader by the end of the document.
pages.body: Example: write a two-sentence summary that keeps the main claim and one qualification. The goal concerns a written artifact rather than a certificate or score.
pages.detail: Working record: Write a goal you can check against a short piece of your own writing. Keep your first attempt and your revised version so the change remains visible.
pages.question: Write a goal you can check against a short piece of your own writing.

pages.title: Pick a route through the practice.
pages.lead: Choose a route based on your focus while retaining the same final reflection. Route A starts with the main claim; route B starts with examples; route C starts with uncertainty.
pages.body: Suggested route A: pages 4, 5, 6, 9, 10. Route B: pages 5, 4, 7, 9, 10. Route C: pages 6, 7, 8, 9, 10. You can revisit any page.
pages.subheading: Route A / route B / route C / return point
pages.detail: Working record: Choose a route and name the reason it fits your present question. Keep your first attempt and your revised version so the change remains visible.
pages.question: Choose a route and name the reason it fits your present question.

pages.title: Take a note that separates roles.
pages.lead: Label the main claim, supporting example and qualification in an invented passage. Notes are easier to reuse when they preserve these distinctions.
pages.body: Passage: A shared sketch may focus a conversation; for example, a speaker can point to a shape. This depends on the discussion task. The final sentence qualifies the first.
pages.detail: Working record: Make a three-part note without turning may into will. Keep your first attempt and your revised version so the change remains visible.
pages.question: Make a three-part note without turning may into will.

pages.title: Try a summary station.
pages.lead: Write a short summary of the passage using fewer words while preserving its uncertainty. Concision should not erase the condition that makes the claim accurate.
pages.body: Possible draft: A shared sketch can provide a common reference, but its usefulness depends on the task. This is a summary of an invented passage, not a research finding.
pages.subheading: Original idea / shorter wording / retained condition
pages.detail: Working record: Write your own two-sentence summary and underline its qualification. Keep your first attempt and your revised version so the change remains visible.
pages.question: Write your own two-sentence summary and underline its qualification.

pages.title: Review with a feedback key.
pages.lead: Compare the meaning of your summary with the source passage. The key checks whether a claim, example or condition disappeared; it does not assign a grade.
pages.body: If your draft says shared sketches improve all discussions, it has expanded the original claim. If it merely lists a shape, it may have retained the example but lost the main idea.
pages.subheading: Claim retained / example handled / condition retained
pages.detail: Working record: Identify one expansion or omission in your draft and explain its effect. Keep your first attempt and your revised version so the change remains visible.
pages.question: Identify one expansion or omission in your draft and explain its effect.

pages.title: Use a targeted support page.
pages.lead: Return to the step that caused difficulty rather than restarting the whole course. A support exercise should address a specific confusion.
pages.body: If examples dominate your notes, highlight only the sentence that makes the general claim. If uncertainty disappears, copy the conditional phrase before writing a new summary.
pages.detail: Working record: Choose one support move and use it on the same passage. Keep your first attempt and your revised version so the change remains visible.
pages.question: Choose one support move and use it on the same passage.

pages.title: Apply the method to a new passage.
pages.lead: Transfer the reading routine to another invented statement. Keep the main claim and its boundary visible instead of borrowing the conclusion from the earlier example.
pages.body: New passage: offering several texts might invite different interests; however, a discussion needs a way to share references. Identify the claim and the condition before summarising.
pages.detail: Working record: Write a fresh summary and note one difference from the shared-sketch passage. Keep your first attempt and your revised version so the change remains visible.
pages.question: Write a fresh summary and note one difference from the shared-sketch passage.

pages.title: Collect the learning artifacts.
pages.lead: Bring your first note, first summary, feedback note and revised summary together. A small portfolio makes the route visible even when you took the pages out of order.
pages.body: Label each artifact by version, not an invented completion date. Include one line explaining why the revised version better matches the source.
pages.detail: Working record: Select four artifacts and arrange them so another reader can follow the revision. Keep your first attempt and your revised version so the change remains visible.
pages.question: Select four artifacts and arrange them so another reader can follow the revision.

pages.title: Choose the next route.
pages.lead: Reflect on the step that became clearer and the difficulty that remains. The next route should follow from that observation rather than a generic instruction to practise more.
pages.body: You might continue with conditional claims, compare two passages or practise separating examples from explanations. No result about real learner performance is supplied by this template.
pages.subheading: Clearer step / remaining difficulty / next practice
pages.detail: Working record: Name one next practice task and the artifact you will use to review it. Keep your first attempt and your revised version so the change remains visible.
pages.question: Name one next practice task and the artifact you will use to review it.
